headline: Moderna turns profitable and raises its revenue outlook
summary_short: Moderna's Q3 2026 revenue was $1.3 billion, up 29% y/y, and it posted net income of $162 million versus a $200 million loss a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue growth came mainly from higher COVID vaccine sales in international markets under long-term government partnerships ($780 million U.S., $533 million international). R&D fell 27% to $583 million on lower late-stage clinical costs. Cash and investments reached $8.0 billion, helped by $2.6 billion of net convertible note proceeds and offset by a $950 million litigation settlement payment. Guidance now calls for 15%-25% revenue growth in 2026, up from up to 10%, and year-end cash of $8.1-$8.3 billion.
confidence_notes: Q/q revenue comparison is distorted by the strongly seasonal Q2 base ($145M). Cash and investments ($8.0B) is the release's definition and differs from the shard's cash-equivalents-only line. Guidance recorded in summary text only; no guidance array written to the shard (no sanctioned script).

drivers.explanation: Primarily higher COVID vaccine sales in international markets, supported by deliveries under long-term strategic government partnerships.
Rose primarily on higher product sales volume and other manufacturing-related costs; includes $65 million of third-party royalties.
A $362 million improvement y/y; the release links it to higher revenue and R&D that fell 27% on lower late-stage clinical development costs.
Increase primarily reflected $2.6 billion net proceeds from convertible notes and capped calls, partly offset by the $950 million litigation settlement payment and cash used in operations.
Management raised 2026 revenue growth expectations to 15%-25% and improved its GAAP operating expense outlook by about $0.2 billion.
